conventions.convention: The potential is C4 on a supplied open collision-free domain. A regular MEP has nonzero derivative everywhere, including one-sided endpoint derivatives, and satisfies (I−ttᵀ)∇V=0. Fixed endpoints need not be minima.
Hessian eigenvalues are ordered increasingly. Index one with gap γ requires λ1≤−γ and every remaining eigenvalue ≥γ; interval enclosures require independently validated evidence.

The HVP truncation constant bounds the third derivative of each gradient coordinate restricted to the entire dimer segment; the estimate concerns the supplied direction, not a full matrix operator error.
The Euclidean residual lemma uses r=2βε only when ε>0. Its zero-residual branch asserts a root without asserting uniqueness.
The maximum-norm lemma instead permits ε=0 and a chosen positive radius r satisfying βε≤r/2; its uniqueness conclusion includes this case.
Closed-interval C3 curves extend to an open parameter interval; endpoint derivatives are continuous one-sided values. Sampling is by unit-speed arc length.
Equal neighboring energies select the centered-chord NEB tie branch. Climbing starts at k=n_climb; tolerance testing precedes budget exhaustion, including at N=0.

The gauge-fixed comparison uses maximum absolute scalar coordinates for both residual and node norms, a fixed local normal-frame convention, and mesh-independent inverse and derivative-Lipschitz bounds.

load_bearing.statement: A regular minimum-energy path has fixed endpoints, nonvanishing derivative, and satisfies (I−t(s)t(s)ᵀ)∇V(R(s))=0 for every parameter value.

For a C1 square residual with invertible A=DF(x0), inverse bound β, positive residual ε, r=2βε, doubled ball in the domain, and βLr≤1/2, there is exactly one zero in the closed radius-r Euclidean ball.

For the stated unit-speed C3 curve and coordinate third-derivative bound, centered derivative error is at most M3h²/6 and unequal-step derivative error is at most M3h−h+/6; when this bound is at most 1/2, normalization is defined and tangent error is at most four times that bound.
Under the stated C4, whole-segment, coordinate derivative, and gradient-error assumptions, the computed central HVP error is at most √d M4 ε²/6 + η/ε.

A validated index-one gap γ, HVP error δ≤γ/4, accepted rotation residual τ_rot, and measured Rayleigh estimate ≤−γ/2 imply sin angle(v,q1)≤4(τ_rot+δ)/(5γ). The nearby-saddle conclusion additionally requires the stated gradient-residual and Hessian-Lipschitz ball conditions.

Under its square C1 residual, inverse bound β, chosen positive radius r, βε≤r/2, doubled-domain ball, and βLr≤1/2 hypotheses, there is exactly one zero in the closed maximum-norm ball, at distance at most 2βε, including ε=0.

Under the stated regular C3 unit-speed MEP, derivative, mesh, and gradient bounds, centered-tangent projected force is O(h²), equal-spacing spring residual is O(h³), and equal-length polyline redistribution moves exact samples by O(h²).
